title: client-voice-docket-and-feature-spark-jan-2029
body:
Purpose: informal roll-up of recent field calls (Dec 2028–Jan 2029), lightweight synthesis of recurring asks, and a set of small experiments / quick-fix proposals we can ship in 2–6 weeks. Intended for triage with Product (hosted-api + console) and Eng (serving-runtime) teams.

Summary (top 4 recurring themes)
1) Prompt-aware cost visibility: customers want per-route token cost split by prompt template/role. "We can’t tell which prompt is burning credit" (Large SaaS org). Impact: high for cost-sensitive scale customers.
2) Graceful degrade for KV-cache misses: several partners reported tail-latency spikes when cold-starting long-running chat sessions. Request: transparent fallback to slightly-lower-quality model variant or cached response while warmup occurs.
3) Embedding drift detection + auto-sample: customers building semantic search ask for an early-warning when embeddings drift vs baseline (monthly) and a one-click resample plan.
4) Self-serve rollout controls in Console: granular canary targeting (by user cohort, route header, region) and an audit trail export for compliance reviews.

Raw customer snippets (pulled from calls/slack/zendesk)
- "Our agents spike cost when the embedded system re-runs prompts for each turn — we need per-template costs." — Fintech partner, NA
- "When we hit morning traffic, latency balloons for some sessions and we lose customers mid-flow." — Retail marketplace
- "We want a safe way to test a model swap for 1% of users and log the diff for SOC review." — Health tech

Quick-fix proposals (1–6 weeks)
A. Prompt-template cost breakdown (MVP) — priority medium-high
   - What: augment Console usage table to include top-10 prompt templates by cost, derived from route+prompt-hash sampling.
   - Data approach: sample 1/1000 requests streaming token counts and map to hashed prompt templates.
   - Acceptance: product can show top-10 and a CSV export; accuracy ~95% for heavy routes.
   - Owner: Priya Nair (prod) + Ethan Chu (analytics)

B. Cold-session degrade policy (experiment) — priority high
   - What: runtime policy that returns from a warm replica or a quantized variant under tight latency windows; flag in request metadata when applied.
   - Risks: potential quality regression, must be opt-in per customer.
   - Metrics: tail latency (p95/p99), quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE proxy on a small eval set), customer drop-off rate.
   - Quick rollout: dark-launch for 5 pilot customers (JIRA-2148).

C. Embedding drift sampler (MVP) — priority medium
   - What: nightly job that computes cosine-similarity distribution vs baseline; if median similarity < threshold, surface alert in Console and create a resample runbook link.
   - Owner: Rafael Ortiz (solutions eng)

D. Canary targeting v0 (console UX patch) — priority medium-low
   - What: allow canary by header match and tag; exportable audit trace with user IDs redacted.
   - Short-term: support for header-based targeting only (no cohort builder).

Proposed prioritization rationale (one-pager style)
- High business impact + implementable: Cold-session degrade policy (B) — reduces customer churn from latency tails immediately.
- High visibility + moderate cost to build: Prompt-template cost breakdown (A) — helps power usage conversations and reduce bill shock.
- Medium ROI but important for search customers: Embedding drift sampler (C).
- UX polish that unblocks compliance reviews: Canary targeting v0 (D).

Open questions / things to validate (notes-to-self)
- How noisy will prompt-template hashing be for templated vs free-text prompts? (ask inference telemetry team)
- For degrade policy, what model variants are safe for health/finance customers? Need legal/security sign-off for auto-fallback behavior.
- Do we have retention on the token-count stream > 7 days for sampling? If not, what is cost?
- Who owns the audit export privacy review? (cc: security-and-compliance)

Cross-team asks (who to loop in)
- Product: confirm UX priority for the cost table + CSV export (Priya)
- Eng-serving-runtime: feasibility of runtime fallback flags and opt-in per-customer (SRE impact)
- Applied-ML: define small quality eval set for each pilot customer for degrade experiments
- Security: privacy review for audit exports and fallback metadata flags

Mini prioritization matrix (text form)
- Impact: High/Medium/Low across themes.
- Effort: S/M/L (estimate)
   Prompt-cost (A): Impact=Medium-High, Effort=S
   Cold-degrade (B): Impact=High, Effort=M-L
   Embedding-sampler (C): Impact=Medium, Effort=S-M
   Canary-v0 (D): Impact=Medium, Effort=S

Quick timeline (draft)
- Week 0–1: align owners + technical spike for B and A (telemetry check)
- Week 2–3: implement A sampling + Console view (MVP) and start dark-launch for B with 2 customers
- Week 4–5: expand B pilots to 5 customers; ship C nightly job prototype
- Week 6: ship A CSV export; evaluate metrics and decide on scaling

Acceptance criteria (short)
- A: Console shows top-10 prompt templates, CSV export present, sampled data link to example rows
- B: Fallback policy toggled per-customer, flagging in logs, no >5% quality regression on pilot eval sets
- C: Nightly alert triggers and resample runbook link in Console
- D: Canary header targeting + export for audit

Notes / side-ideas (brainstorm fragments)
- Could attach a small usage-cost forecast widget to the prompt table (proj savings if trimmed by 10%)
- Provide an automated suggestion: "Consider compressing user instructions" when a template crosses 1k tokens routinely
- Explore using reservoir sampling on request bodies to keep storage cost low

Next steps (immediate)
- Sync with Priya + Ethan on telemetry feasibility (by 2029-02-08)
- Triage JIRA-2148 into B pilot plan and identify 2 pilot customers (owner: Rafael)
- Draft short customer comms for opt-in baseline quality notices (Sofia)

Appendix: draft slack snippets to surface to Eng/Product
- "Heads-up: repeated reports of p99 session latency causing user drop. Proposal: runtime fallback to quantized variant for cold sessions (dark-launch). See JIRA-2148 for context and pilot plan."
- "Quick win: add top-10 prompt template cost breakdown in Console — low-effort sampling spike to help customers reduce bill surprises."

-- end of docket --

(rough notes; will convert to a tidy playbook if triage says go)
